name: Split Flap Text
description: Airport-style split-flap display that flips tile by tile through random glyphs to reveal each phrase, then cycles through a list of phrases, with adjustable depth, glare and tile styling.
contents: Row of flip tiles, one per character, padded to a fixed width
Screen-reader-only label with the current phrase
Inline stylesheet with keyframes for flap, shade, glare and reveal
behavior: Each tile flips through random glyphs from the charset before landing on the target character
Tiles start in a cascade from left, right or center with a stagger delay
Cycles through the words list after a hold delay, optionally looping
Optional intro flips in the first phrase from blank tiles
Respects prefers-reduced-motion by skipping flap animation
Depth controls shading, hinge and shadow strength, glare adds a sheen on flipping flaps
editableByProps: Phrases to show (words array or single text), alignment and minimum tile count
Tile and text colors, radius, gap and font size
Flip speed, stagger, hold time, flips per character, charset, cascade order, looping and intro
Depth and glare intensity, board or minimal tile look

needsCodeEdit.where: .split-flap-text rule in the styles template literal

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the flip easing or keyframe motion
needsCodeEdit.where: split-flap-front and split-flap-back keyframes in the styles constant

fixed: Root is an inline-flex row with no frame, so it sits at the start of its parent and is not centered by itself
Injects a style tag with global class names prefixed split-flap-text
Tiles are fixed-width flex items sized from fontSize and never wrap, so long phrases or large fontSize overflow horizontally on small screens, reduce fontSize or padTo there
Phrases longer than the tile width are cut, width is the larger of padTo and the longest phrase
Uses a monospace font stack and a hardcoded tile shadow and gradient look
Extra props are spread onto the root div
Uses color-mix in CSS, requiring a modern browser

options.look: Solid dark tiles with gradient, hinge line, shadow and 3D flap rotation
options.useWhen: A hero headline or status board that should look like a physical airport departures display

options.look: Transparent tiles with only a thin split line and a clip-path reveal of glyphs, no tile background
options.useWhen: A large headline over a photo or colored section where the text should flip without visible tile boxes
